prompt: Centre text inside a fixed-width field, putting the odd leftover pad character on the right. Complete center and centerBlock, then run the tests.
explanation: The total padding is width minus the text length; integer division by 2 gives the left share and the remainder (total - left) becomes the right share, which is why the extra character lands on the right. Guarding with text.length() >= width first keeps the method from computing a negative repeat count. String.repeat(n) from Java 11 builds each run of padding in one call, and centerBlock simply reuses center for every line.
hints: Return text unchanged first if it is already width characters or longer -- otherwise repeat() would be asked for a negative count.
left = (width - text.length()) / 2, and right is whatever is left over: total - left.
String.valueOf(pad).repeat(left) builds the padding; centerBlock can just call center in a loop and put "\n" between results.
